name: Slingsby T67 Firefly
summary: British side-by-side aerobatic trainer derived from the Fournier RF-6B, built in composite and used by the RAF, USAF as the T-3A and flying schools; ex-service examples are now privately owned.

wings: Low, straight tapered wing with rounded tips
Composite (GRP) construction with a smooth finish
engines: Single Lycoming flat-four (or Continental) with a two or three-blade propeller
fuselage: Large bubble canopy over side-by-side seats
Fixed tricycle gear with wheel fairings
Smooth fuselage tapering to the tail
tail: Horizontal tail mounted on the rear fuselage

tellTales: Big bubble canopy over side-by-side seats on a smooth composite low-wing
Fixed tricycle gear with wheel fairings and a swept fin

confusedWith.howToTell: The Bulldog is an angular metal airplane with a tall swept fin; the Firefly is a smooth composite with a more rounded look.
The DA20 has a more rounded canopy and fuselage with a T-tail-like profile; the Firefly has a bigger bubble and a slimmer body.
The P-Mentor is a metal-and-carbon trainer with a different canopy; the Firefly is an all-composite with a larger bubble canopy.
